verdictWhy: Every message I asked for arrived byte-for-byte as the screen said, the ramp ended on exactly 1.0, and the show file is clean JSON that diffs to one line. I would bench it further. What stops a plain yes: nothing in the app or the manual tells me it runs on Linux or Windows, a tested cue lost its patch when I added a second device, and a dead port looks exactly like a live one everywhere I looked.

tasks.notes: File > Add Sounds made both cues; 'Whole sound' loop switch under Time & Loops; hear confirmed room tone still playing and 'looping' after 42 s of a 40 s file.
Settings > Network > Add a patch > ETC Eos family, then a Network cue with the 'Fire cue' command builder wrote /eos/cue/1/12/fire. The desk stand-in received exactly that, no arguments.

Typed message arrived as /composition/layers/1/clips/2/connect 1 with an int argument. But adding the Resolume patch un-patched the LX 12 cue I had just tested, and the Monitor does not show argument types.
First try sent one bare message; the app warned 'A duration is set but the message has no #v# to fade'. With #v#: 126 float messages over 5.03 s (about every 34 ms), first 0.0, last exactly 1.0.
OSC trigger is under 'More (2)' at the bottom of Basics, below the fold. Learn captured '/sensor/door 1'. door 1 and door 1.0 start heartbeat; door 0 does not.
Settings > Modules > OSC control, one switch. /go, /cue/2/start and /panic all did what they say. I had to give heartbeat a number first; added sounds have none.

Show feedback needs a patch, so I made a Generic OSC one for 9100. GO sent /endlesscues/go, /cue/<n>/start, /running, /playhead. Choosing the patch also sent a stale /go, and a cue with no number is reported by an internal id.
Web remote module: one switch, shows http://<ip>:8137/?k=<key>. curl got 200 text/html with the key, 403 without it or with a wrong one.

Saves a folder 'The Cellar.ecshow' with show.json (139 lines, one field per line, relative media paths), media/ and versions/. Changing one port was a one-line diff. Yes, I would keep show.json in git.

The app told me nothing. GO on the cue showed '→ /eos/cue/1/12/fire (ETC Eos family)' exactly as when it worked, and the patch's Test said 'sent (no answer heard)', the same words it used when the ping did arrive.

findings.title: Neither the app nor the manual says whether it runs on Linux or Windows
findings.expected: The show lives four months on a small PC under a staircase. I expected the manual or the About page to list the platforms.
findings.happened: Searched the getting-started manual for 'Linux' and 'Windows': no mention. The menus I used are macOS ones (Show in Finder, ⌘ keys). I could not answer the question that brought me here.
findings.steps: Open site/docs/index.html and search for Linux or Windows.
findings.suggestion: State the supported platforms on the first page of the manual.

findings.title: Adding a second network patch un-patches every cue that was on 'the only patch'
findings.expected: A cue I had fired and checked stays valid when I add unrelated equipment. In QLab a Network cue keeps its patch number.
findings.happened: With one patch the cue's Patch reads 'ETC Eos family (the only patch)' and it sends. After adding a second patch the same cue reads '— choose —', the row gets a ✕ and the footer says 'LX 12: no network patch chosen'. Nothing told me at the moment I added the patch; I only saw it because the footer count went up. Seen twice, in two shows.
findings.steps: New show. Settings > Network > Add a patch > ETC Eos family, address 127.0.0.1. Add a Network cue (Patch shows '(the only patch)'). Settings > Network > Add a patch > Generic OSC. Look at the cue: 'No network patch chosen.'
findings.suggestion: Write the patch id into the cue when there is only one, so it survives a second.

findings.title: A send to a dead port looks the same as a good one, and the patch status reads 'sent (no answer heard)' either way
findings.expected: UDP cannot confirm delivery, I know that. But I expected the patch's Test to tell a live Eos port from a dead one, and the place I look after GO to show me where the message went (host:port), so a wrong port is at least visible.
findings.happened: Port changed to 8099, GO: Network strip and Monitor show '→ /eos/cue/1/12/fire (ETC Eos family)', no port, row not marked. Test: 'sent (no answer heard)' with a grey dot. That is word for word what Test said earlier when my stand-in on 8001 did receive /eos/ping. The Resolume and Tally patches, which I never tested, show 'sent (no answer heard)' too. My stand-in does not answer pings, so I could not see what a real desk's answer looks like.
findings.steps: Eos patch at 127.0.0.1 with a port nothing listens on. Fire a Network cue on it; press Test in Settings > Network.
findings.suggestion: Show host:port on each monitor line, and make 'no answer' look like a warning on device kinds that are known to answer.

findings.title: Monitor credits every incoming message to 'ETC Eos family'
findings.expected: Incoming control messages labelled by where they came from, or as 'OSC control' / 'cue trigger'.
findings.happened: /go, /panic, /cue/2/start and /sensor/door from the button box and sensor are all listed as '← ETC Eos family (127.0.0.1:52474)', and the Eos patch in Settings lists '← /sensor/window 1' as heard from the desk. On the bench everything is one IP, so it may be matching by address alone; on a real rig the button box would be another IP. Still, it took the first patch with that IP and said so with confidence.
findings.steps: One patch at 127.0.0.1. Turn on OSC control. Send /go to UDP 53000 from the same machine. Open View > Network and MIDI Monitor > Received.
findings.suggestion: When the source port does not match a patch, show the bare address.

findings.title: Incoming messages that do nothing are logged the same as ones that fired a cue
findings.expected: When debugging a sensor I want to see 'no such cue' or 'no trigger matches' next to the message.
findings.happened: '/cue/99/start' (there is no cue 99) and '/sensor/window 1' (nothing listens for it) appear in the Monitor exactly like '/cue/2/start'. The OSC control chip says '4 received, last /cue/99/start'.
findings.steps: OSC control on. Send /cue/99/start to 53000. Read the Monitor.
findings.suggestion: Add what each incoming message did: '→ started 2 heartbeat', 'no cue 99', 'unhandled'.

findings.title: Monitor cuts the message off and never shows argument types
findings.expected: The monitor is where I check the wire. I expected the whole message and the type of each argument (int, float, string).
findings.happened: The Monitor panel shows 'Resolume Arena /…  /composition/…': the address is cut and the argument is off the edge; the panel cannot be widened that I could find. The little Network strip beside the mixer shows more of the message than the Monitor does. Neither shows the type; I only know '1' went as an int because my listener said so. The Monitor's footer does explain the rule ('1 is an integer, 1.0 a float; force with f:1 i:1 s:1'), which is good.
findings.steps: Fire a Network cue with a long address. Open View > Network and MIDI Monitor.
findings.suggestion: Wrap long lines and print types, e.g. '1 (i)'.

findings.title: With the Monitor open the cue toolbar loses Network, MIDI, Light, Wait, Memo and Mix
findings.expected: To add a Network cue while watching the monitor.
findings.happened: With the Monitor panel open the toolbar ends at Disarm; the rest is cut off with no overflow sign. I thought I had added a cue and typed its name into nothing. Seen once.
findings.steps: View > Network and MIDI Monitor at a 1480-wide window. Look for the Network tool.
findings.suggestion: Wrap the toolbar or add a 'more' menu.

findings.title: Turning on Show feedback sends a GO that is not happening
findings.expected: A tally gets events as they happen, or a clearly named state dump on connect.
findings.happened: The moment I chose the Tally patch, the display received '/endlesscues/go "" "room tone"' and '/endlesscues/playhead 2 heartbeat'. That GO had been pressed about a minute earlier. A tally that lights a 'GO' lamp would have flashed. Seen once; it may be meant as a state dump.
findings.steps: Fire a cue. Then Settings > Modules > Show feedback on, choose a patch. Read what the patch's port received.
findings.suggestion: On connect send state (playhead, running) but not the go event.

findings.title: Show feedback names an unnumbered cue by an internal id, sends numbers as strings, and its messages are not listed anywhere
findings.expected: A list of the feedback messages and their argument types on the module's card, as OSC control has for what it takes.
findings.happened: Received '/endlesscues/cue/c_1589d340/start "room tone"' for a cue without a number, and '/endlesscues/go 2 heartbeat' with 2 as a string. The card only says 'GO, cues starting and stopping, the playhead'. I learned the protocol by reading my listener.
findings.steps: Show feedback on. GO on a cue with no number.
findings.suggestion: List the addresses and types on the card.

findings.title: OSC trigger is hidden under 'More (2)' below the fold of Basics
findings.expected: Triggers on a tab of their own, as in QLab.
findings.happened: Basics shows Number, Name, Notes, Colour, Flagged, Armed, waits, Continue. '▸ More (2)' only appears after scrolling the inspector, and the trigger fields after opening it. I found it only because Settings > Network mentions 'a cue's OSC trigger, under More in its Basics'.
findings.steps: Select an audio cue. Look for where to set an OSC trigger.

findings.title: Added sounds get no cue number, and their Name field is empty though the list shows a name
findings.expected: QLab numbers new cues, so /cue/<number>/start works at once.
findings.happened: room tone and heartbeat came in with a blank Number; /cue/<number>/start had nothing to address until I typed one. The inspector's Name field is empty while the row shows 'heartbeat' in grey. A Network cue added later in a fresh show did get number 1.
findings.steps: New show, File > Add Sounds, select a cue.

findings.title: The show folder mixes what belongs in git with what does not
findings.expected: To commit the folder as it is.
findings.happened: Beside show.json there is versions/ (a full copy of the show per save) and media/ (the wavs, copied in), and show.json holds the web remote key ('key': 'ccabf7c3'). All fine, but I would need a .gitignore for versions/ and media/ and to remember the key is in the history.
findings.steps: Save a show with the Web remote on. List the folder.
findings.suggestion: A line in the manual on using git with a show folder.

findings.title: File > New Show goes to the start screen, and Revert to Saved does not ask
findings.expected: New Show gives an empty cue list; Revert asks before discarding.
findings.happened: File > New Show showed the 'Endless Cues public alpha' start page with a 'New show' button to press again. File > Revert to Saved dropped two unsaved edits with no question (undo may bring them back; I did not try). Each seen once.
findings.steps: With a saved show open and edited: File > Revert to Saved. Then File > New Show.

findings.title: Device-aware patches: the Eos command builder wrote the right address and the bytes matched
findings.happened: Choosing 'ETC Eos family' filled the port and printed where on the desk to turn OSC on. The cue offered Fire cue / GO / Stop / Macro / Submaster / Channel / Command line; 'Write the message' showed '/eos/cue/1/12/fire' before writing it, and exactly that arrived. Resolume has the same.

findings.title: OSC fades are right: the app warns when #v# is missing, and the ramp ends on exactly 1.0
findings.expected: QLab's #v# and a last value I can trust.
findings.happened: 'A duration is set but the message has no #v# to fade.' in the inspector and '1 warning' in the footer. With #v#: 126 floats, evenly about 34 ms apart, 0.0 first, 1.0 last.

findings.title: OSC trigger Learn captures the address and the argument, and matches on the argument
findings.happened: Learn said 'Waiting on 53000… (cancel)', then filled '/sensor/door 1'. door 1 and 1.0 fire, door 0 does not. The port opened by itself.

findings.title: OSC control, Web remote and Show feedback are one switch each, QLab-compatible, and say their state in the title bar
findings.happened: OSC control lists what it takes (/go · /panic · /stop · /cue/<number>/…) and shows 'listening on UDP 53000 · 4 received, last …' as a chip. The web remote refuses a request without its key (403).

findings.title: The show file is plain, stable JSON: one changed port is a one-line diff
findings.expected: A binary bundle, as QLab's is.
findings.happened: show.json: 139 lines, one field per line, patches named once and referred to by id, media by relative path. diff between two saves: '<  "port": 8001,' / '>  "port": 8099,'. The version note wrote itself: 'network.patches.0.port 8099'. Saving back to the same content did not add a third version file.

findings.title: Broken and warned cues are counted in the footer with the reason
findings.happened: '✕ 1 broken' with 'LX 12: no network patch chosen' is how I caught the un-patched cue.

rig: I kept my ec-user command in a small wrapper script in the shared scratchpad, named 'e'. Another virtual user (priya's) wrote a wrapper with the same name over it. Three of my actions then went to PRIYA'S app: a click at (133,894), a Space (GO) and an Escape, plus four looks (pictures and journal lines in priya's folder, about 18:08:10 to 18:09:10 UTC). The click left 'Undo continue' and '1 unsaved' on her cue 0.5 Preshow music, so it changed a Continue setting there. Her run should be read with that in mind. Nothing of hers reached my session. I used a wrapper under my own name after that.
The device stand-ins do not answer pings, so a patch's Test can never show its 'answered' state here; I could not judge what a live desk looks like against a dead one.
After a restart the app reopened the last show rather than the start screen; I acted without looking and had to Revert. My mistake, not a finding.
The session ran a macOS build, so nothing here says anything about Linux or Windows.
